context:
Start with a research gate, not with package installation or test writing.
Use the current explorer implementation as the source of truth:
`results-explorer/src/App.tsx`, `results-explorer/src/db.ts`,
`results-explorer/src/lib/duckdbQueries.ts`, the current page-level Vitest
coverage, and the archived/manual browser-validation notes.

Prefer a Playwright-style browser harness because this item needs
multi-browser support, downloads, clipboard checks, traces, and stable
route-level acceptance. Run against the built explorer rather than mocked
fetches or jsdom-only abstractions. Generate fixture data from canonical
bundles plus controlled mutations in an isolated test area instead of relying
on whatever happens to be present in `results-explorer/public/data/`.

Implement in thin slices:
1. lock architecture in the research gate
2. establish harness and fixture generation
3. land browse-surface happy paths
4. land compare/detail happy paths
5. land query-workbench happy paths
6. add injected failure-path coverage
7. wire CI and residual manual release checks
description:
The results explorer now has substantial unit, component, and parity coverage
under `results-explorer/src/__tests__/` and `results-explorer/src/**/__tests__/`,
but there is still no durable browser-level acceptance suite for the behaviors
that matter most in production:

- real DuckDB-WASM startup and worker loading
- client-side routing under the `/results/` base path
- deep links to ResultDetail / Compare / Query pages
- clipboard and download flows
- compare hard-block and soft-warning behaviors
- query workbench read-only SQL behavior in a real browser
- network and sidecar failure handling

The repo also contains evidence that this gap is real, not hypothetical:
`_project/_archive/handoffs/handoff-results-publishing-phase2.md` explicitly
notes that cross-browser acceptance remained largely manual, and
`verify-trust-badge-rendering-in-explorer` proved that one-off Playwright-driven
browser checks are useful but too narrow and too manual to act as a long-term
quality gate.

This item implements a deterministic browser-functional-test layer for
`results-explorer/`, centered on a Playwright-style harness that runs against
a built explorer app plus generated fixture data. The implementation must not
start by guessing at unresolved details. A research gate comes first and must
lock the execution model, fixture strategy, and browser matrix before any test
or product code is edited.

anti_patterns.dont: begin implementation before the research gate closes the open questions
anti_patterns.why: the built-app target, fixture location, and browser matrix materially change the shape of the solution

anti_patterns.dont: make all three browsers blocking before flake characteristics are known
anti_patterns.instead: require Chromium first and graduate Firefox/WebKit based on research-gate evidence.
anti_patterns.why: a noisy gate will stall adoption

anti_patterns.dont: mutate `results-data/bundles/` or the committed curated corpus to create edge cases
anti_patterns.instead: synthesize variants in an isolated fixture workspace.
anti_patterns.why: that pollutes real published data with test-only scenarios

anti_patterns.dont: point the browser suite at ad-hoc mocked JSON or a jsdom-only harness
anti_patterns.instead: run against generated `results.duckdb` and actual built assets.
anti_patterns.why: the missing coverage is specifically real browser DuckDB-WASM, routing, clipboard, and download behavior

anti_patterns.dont: rely on whichever artifacts happen to exist in `results-explorer/public/data/`
anti_patterns.instead: generate a fixture corpus per run.
anti_patterns.why: the working tree is not deterministic and may not include the variants needed for coverage

preserves.behavior: Existing Vitest unit/component/parity tests remain the fast inner-loop signal; the browser suite supplements them and does not replace them.
Existing result download URLs and compare URL semantics remain shareable and user-facing.
The curated public corpus under `results-data/bundles/` is not modified for browser-test-only edge cases.
The explorer continues to run correctly under the `/results/` base path and existing deep links remain valid.
The query workbench remains read-only against the DuckDB snapshot; browser-test plumbing must not introduce a writable test-only bypass.

work_units.notes:
Read the current explorer routes, DuckDB-WASM loading path, existing
jsdom/unit coverage, manual browser-verification TODOs, and deploy/base-path
assumptions before changing any code.

The research gate must answer all open questions below with explicit
decisions and evidence from the current repo:
- built app vs dev server test target
- temp fixture corpus vs mutating `results-explorer/public/data/`
- blocking vs smoke browser matrix
- minimum seam required for deterministic failure injection

Deliverable: an implementation note at
`docs/development/browser-test-architecture.md` that records the chosen
defaults and rejected alternatives for each open question, plus a link
to it from this TODO's notes before w2 starts. No implementation starts
until these decisions are locked.

Architecture note (accepted 2026-04-18):
`docs/development/browser-test-architecture.md`. Locked decisions:
(1) test target is the built `dist/` served via Playwright `webServer`,
(2) fixture corpus is generated per-run into gitignored
`results-explorer/test-fixtures/.generated/` with the curated public
corpus untouched, (3) Chromium full suite is the required blocking
gate while Firefox and WebKit run `@smoke` only and graduate on flake
data, (4) no production-code seam is added for failure injection -
all error paths are exercised through Playwright `page.route()`,
`setOffline`, permissions grants, and download events.
work_units.summary: Run a research gate and lock the browser-test architecture before editing

work_units.notes:
Add the test runner, package scripts, `playwright.config.ts`, and failure
artifact handling. The suite must exercise the built explorer with the
real `/results/` base path rather than a mocked or simplified route setup.

Required harness properties:
- deterministic local command for one-shot setup + run
- traces/screenshots/report on failure
- artifact directories gitignored
- Chromium as the primary gate from the first slice
work_units.summary: Add the browser-test harness, scripts, and built-app serving model

work_units.notes:
Browser tests must not depend on whichever derived artifacts happen to be
present in the working tree. Generate fixture data per run from canonical
source bundles plus controlled metadata variants so tests can cover:
- valid compare cohorts
- mixed trust labels
- mixed tuning modes
- multiple phases / execution modes
- results with and without tuning sidecars
- compare-invalid cohorts for hard-block tests

The generated fixture corpus must be isolated from `results-data/bundles/`
and from the committed curated corpus.
work_units.summary: Implement deterministic fixture-corpus generation for browser tests

- Home
- BenchmarkIndex
- PlatformIndex

Cover real interactions rather than only page load:
- filter toggles and URL sync
- route deep-link loads
- result and cohort navigation

Keep this slice limited to the landing and browse surfaces so it can land
as a single vertical increment without being blocked on compare, query,

work_units.summary: Cover Home plus benchmark/platform index happy paths under the real `/results/` base path

Cover real interactions rather than only page load:

work_units.summary: Cover ResultDetail and Compare happy paths, deep links, and shareable URL-state workflows

work_units.notes:
Add browser tests for the Query page that prove the browser-only parts of
the workbench against a real built app:
- query-table sorting and column toggles
- starter-query loading
- read-only SQL enforcement in the workbench
- CSV and JSON download flows

Keep this separate from the route-browse and compare slices because Query
already has several distinct behaviors in Vitest and is large enough to
justify its own work unit.
work_units.summary: Cover Query workbench browser workflows, read-only SQL, and table/download interactions

work_units.notes:
Add explicit tests for the behaviors jsdom does not prove today:
- DuckDB snapshot missing/corrupt or unreachable
- compare benchmark mismatch and scale mismatch hard blocks
- tuning-config sidecar fetch failure
- online/offline or retry-state behavior where supported by the app
- RG-2 HTTP range-reads: assert that a cold single-row lookup against
  `results.duckdb` served by the test harness issues `Range: bytes=...`
  requests, receives `206 Partial Content` with `Accept-Ranges: bytes`,
  and that the sum of `Content-Length` transferred is ≤10% of the
  on-disk DB size. This closes the
  `explorer-canonical-browser-duckdb-read-model` RG-2 gate that the
  completed TODO deferred to browser-level coverage.

Failure assertions must validate user-visible error states, not only
thrown exceptions or console output.
work_units.summary: Cover failure and recovery paths with user-visible assertions

work_units.notes:
Wire the new suite into CI with a stable gating policy:
- Chromium full suite required
- Firefox and WebKit smoke coverage initially narrower unless the
  research gate proves full parity is low-risk
- failure artifacts uploaded in CI

Also document the residual manual release check for meaningful explorer
changes: one short pass across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari for layout and
browser-specific rendering issues that automation may not catch early.
work_units.summary: Integrate the suite into CI and define the release-check browser matrix
